def cheby(r1, c1, r2, c2):
    return max(abs(r1-r2), abs(c1-c2))

def can_reach_via_orthogonal_path_from_start_cell(start_r, start_c, end_r, end_c, grid_val):
    """Can we go from any ortho-3 neighbor of nearest active 2 to this cell via orthogonal path staying on same value?"""
    
    # Find the nearest active two and its ortho-3 neighbors
    min_d = float('inf')
    nearest_active = None
    for ar, ac in active_twos_set:
        d = cheby(start_r, start_c, ar, ac)
        if d < min_d:
            min_d = d
            nearest_active = (ar, ac)
    
    if nearest_active is None or min_d > 1:
        return False
    
    # Get all ortho-3 neighbors of the nearest active two
    target_ortho_cells = ortho_3_neighbors[nearest_active]
    
    # Can we reach the cell from any of these ortho cells via orthogonal path on same value?
    # Use BFS starting from all ortho cells
    from collections import deque
    q = deque(target_ortho_cells)
    visited = set(target_ortho_cells)
    
    while q:
        cr, cc = q.popleft()
        
        # Check all 4 orthogonal neighbors
        for dr, dc in [(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1),(0,1)]:
            nr, nc = cr+dr, cc+dc
            
            if 0 <= nr < rows and 0 <= nc < cols:
                if (nr, nc) == (end_r, end_c):
                    return True
                if (nr, nc) not in visited and grid[nr][nc] == grid_val:
                    visited.add((nr, nc))
                    q.append((nr, nc))
    
    return False
